title: Deployment verification is explicitly outside audit scope and must be a separate review
content:
A.1.10.2.7.1.1.2.1 ends with a boundary statement: "**Deployment verification, including confirmation of address correctness and on-chain state, is not within the scope of an audit of deployment and initialization scripts and must be performed as a separate deployment verification review.**"

The distinction is between a script being correct and a deployment being correct. An audit examines logic: given these parameters, does the library do the right thing? Verification examines a fact: were these the parameters used, is this the resulting on-chain state, is this the right address?

Saying so explicitly prevents a specific and plausible failure. Once code is "audited," everyone downstream tends to treat the deployment as covered, and the actual parameters used on the day — the values that determine what the contract is — end up unexamined because each party assumes the other side handled it. That gap is exactly where an incorrect address or a wrong role grant survives.

The Atlas provides the separate review elsewhere: the Smart Contract Deployment Verification process at A.1.10.2.3.2.1, the Forum post attestations that constructor arguments match the Init script, and the tiered verification requirements at A.1.10.2.5.2.1.1.

There is a general methodological point here worth extracting: a verification artifact should state what it does *not* cover. An audit report with an unstated boundary will be relied on for more than it establishes, and no one will notice until the uncovered part fails.
description: A.1.10.2.7.1.1.2.1 excludes address correctness and on-chain state from script audits, so 'it was audited' can never be read as covering how the code was actually deployed.
